original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: One measured replay bottleneck: the per-output full-triple scans in the joint-dual serialized-word replay (scripts/experiments/binary_frame_replay.replay on certificates/joint-dual-word-{23,25}.json.gz). Replace the O(outputs x v) scans with per-call containment masks in an opt-in adapter, with the frozen historical verifier, its scripts and tests/test_joint_reclaim.py untouched and used as the oracle.
scope_change_reason: Card selection: my first-choice drawn card portable-replay (scope key 831cc1a3c8f9ff01b197) matched the fresh claim of 2026-10-14T11:24Z in discussion 1166 (completed as https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1834), so per the pair-collision rule I took the second-choice card replay-runtime (scope key b1dd41940c60d240b47a, chooser OS nonce 24ae43237c3eaed2410bcdf516d854cd). Refinement inside the card: of the replay stages measurable at base (the isolated test suite, the research-workflow gate, research_package metadata validation, the joint-dual word replay), only the joint-dual word replay had a single dominant, cleanly replaceable measured bottleneck; research_package.py source validation was already batched by research/git-provenance-stream and the research-workflow gate has a flat distribution of subprocess-bound fixtures with no single hotspot.
bottleneck_link: The joint-dual replay is the independent word check for the frame-compiler line from PR 25 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/25) by Rohan Arun (rohanarun, with OpenAI Codex assistance) through PR 58 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/58) by Chafik Boukhalfa (chafreaky, with OpenAI Codex assistance) (research/joint-dual) and the dominant cost of its longest isolated test module (tests/test_joint_reclaim.py). Faster identical-coverage replays shorten the review loop for that line's candidates; this is verification throughput only, not a multiplication mechanism result.
stop_rule: One scan replacement in one adapter; abandon if any receipt differs from the historical implementation or the frozen words, if any mutation outcome differs from the historical oracle, or if paired same-fixture timings show less than a 25 percent reduction on the replay stage. No coverage is removed to reach the target; timings are measurements, never a correctness gate.
evidence: RESULT.json records equal legacy/adapter receipts on both pinned words and their recorded compiler receipts, a full literal-scan cross-check over 12,261 outputs, the frozen 24-case tests/test_joint_reclaim.py mutation matrix against the historical oracle, corrupted-table/unchecked-word/-O controls, and an unmodified frozen-suite adoption run (16 tests) through the shim. BENCHMARK.json records paired timings on two identical fixtures: replay() unit median 2.233s -> 1.285s (1.74x) and the frozen test module 41.47s -> 37.72s (1.10x). Registered replay and --check-only pass; research-workflow tests pass.
author: Aaron Wang

open_questions.question: Can the same containment-mask identity speed up the sibling skip-frame replay line (scripts/experiments/skip_frame_compose.py / verify_skip_frame.py), whose output checks share the triple-scan shape?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The measured 1.74x applies only to the joint-dual replay stage; the skip-frame words (certificates/skip-frame-kappa.json lineage) are a separate frozen chain with their own replay cost.
open_questions.first_step: Profile verify_skip_frame.py on its pinned words, measure the triple-scan share, and if material apply the mask identity behind an adapter cross-checked against that chain's own literal scans and mutation controls.
open_questions.blocked_by: A separate pin freeze and its own oracle controls; this package does not retro-fit or modify any frozen chain.

open_questions.question: Is the remaining full-basis word simulation (M+J+M^-1+V applied twice to all 2v+R basis rows, about 55 percent of the optimized replay) reducible without weakening the independent two-orientation replay?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That loop, not the scans, is now the replay bottleneck; algebraic shortcuts would change the independent-replay character that makes the check trustworthy.
open_questions.first_step: Measure limb traffic and allocation in the two orientation passes on the pinned words and look for a representation change that still executes every XOR of every basis row.
open_questions.blocked_by: The requirement that every basis row of both orientations be executed literally; any shortcut must be justified as an identical check, not a sampled one.

integration_refresh.reason: Current SOURCE.json changes only the joint_dual_reclaim_compiler.py hash; every replay/prepare/test/word input consumed here retains its original bytes. Registered replay is revalidated against this baseline.
